audience.description: GT-571 — WHO the rule is addressed to. 'core' means the rule only makes sense against the Evolith Core monorepo itself (e.g. CLI-RR-01 'run npm run build in sdk/cli', TAX-05 'top-level sdk/, rulesets/') and MUST NOT be evaluated against a satellite; 'satellite' is the mirror image; 'both' (the default, and the reading of any rule that omits the field) keeps the pre-GT-571 behaviour. Declared at ruleset level as the default for its rules, and overridable per rule. A rule excluded by audience is NOT APPLICABLE — it is filtered out before evaluation and is never counted as skipped/checked/errored.

topologies.description: GT-571 — topology ids this rule belongs to (e.g. 'serverless', 'event-driven', 'modular-monolith'). A repository is evaluated against a topology-bound rule only when it declares that topology (metadata.phase F1/F2/F3 or spec.design.topology.confirmed in evolith.yaml). Absent ⇒ topology-agnostic: the rule always applies. Declared at ruleset level as the default for its rules, and overridable per rule.

appliesFromSdlcPhase.description: GT-571 — earliest SDLC phase at which the rule is meaningful: 0=greenfield scaffold ('phase-0', nothing built yet), 1=Conception, 2=Design, 3=Construction, 4=Validation, 5=Delivery. A repository declaring a LOWER phase is not evaluated against the rule, because the artifact the rule inspects does not exist yet. Absent ⇒ the rule applies at every phase (pre-GT-571 behaviour). Gating only happens when the repository actually declares a phase.

enforce.description: How a rule is enforced by an external static analyzer (GT-516 · EAG-10). Additive and optional: a rule with no enforce block is evaluated by the native engine. When engine='enforcer', the PolicyCompiler lowers this block into the tool's native check configuration.

engine.description: 'enforcer' routes to an adapter; 'native'/'opa' stay on their own engine.

tool.description: Enforcer tool that owns this rule (matches an enforcer-catalog.json entry).

toolRuleId.description: The tool's own rule id, when it differs from the Evolith rule id.

runtime.description: Runtime ecosystem the analyzer needs (selects the adapter / gates fallback).

config.description: Tool-native config fragment, inlined (e.g. a dependency-cruiser from/to clause).

configRef.description: Reference to an external tool config, when it is not inlined.

severityMap.description: Maps the tool's own severity vocabulary onto canonical violation severities.

mode.description: Enforcement strength. Defaults from the rule's blocking flag when omitted.

rule.description: A single rule. GT-678 — CLOSED: any key not listed here is rejected with a schema error naming the key and the file, instead of being accepted and silently discarded by the loader (which is how an authored `enabled: false`, or a typo such as `enabeld`, used to produce an unchanged run that looked configured). Add a key here, with its real type, before authoring it.

enabled.description: GT-678 — `false` means the rule is NOT evaluated and the run reports it as disabled with its source (a `notApplicable` entry with reason `disabled` and an `overrides.applied` record). Absent means `true`. Before GT-678 this key was accepted here and silently dropped by the loader, so a tenant that wrote it saw an unchanged run and nothing told them the key was discarded. On a `tenants/**` copy of a Core rule it is part of the per-rule delta (see `approvedBy`/`expiresOn`).

severity.description: MUST | SHOULD | MUST NOT | SHOULD NOT (the loader also accepts COULD/MAY). Absent: derived from `blocking`/`enforcement`.

references.description: Documents, ADRs or standards the rule cites.

assurance.description: How the rule is assured on a topology (topology rulesets).

checklistItem.description: Definition-of-Done checklist wording for the rule.

evidenceRequired.description: Evidence a satellite must present for the rule (CLI rulesets).

sourceFile.description: Authored provenance when the rule was lifted from a source document (security rulesets). Not the loader's `sourceFile`, which is always the ruleset path.

approvedBy.description: GT-678 — who approved this rule's delta. Only meaningful on a `tenants/**` copy of a Core rule: waiving a blocking criterion (`enabled: false` or `blocking: false` on a `blocking: true` Core rule) is rejected with `OVR-BLOCKING-REMOVED` unless BOTH `approvedBy` and `expiresOn` are present; downgrading its severity needs `approvedBy`.

expiresOn.description: GT-678 — the last day a `tenants/**` delta over a Core rule is in force (inclusive, UTC). After it the delta is ignored and reported as `OVR-EXPIRED`. Required, with `approvedBy`, to waive a blocking criterion.
